diagram_name: Read a Freedom Record on the Polygonal Wall
learning_objective: The learner will deconstruct a simplified Delphic manumission record into its eight clauses, naming each clause and judging whether it protects the freed person, limits the freed person's freedom, or records the facts of the sale, with at least 7 of the 8 judgments correct.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** delphi-freedom-record-reader
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** deconstruct
**Learning Objective:** The learner will deconstruct a simplified Delphic manumission record into its eight clauses, naming each clause and judging whether it protects the freed person, limits the freed person's freedom, or records the facts of the sale, with at least 7 of the 8 judgments correct. **Prerequisites:** manumission, manumission records, archon, guarantor, witnesses, paramone, and the sale to the god (all defined in "Manumission Records" above); inscription (Chapter 10); the polygonal wall (defined above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of the eight clauses, the learner commits two answers: the clause name (from eight names) and its effect (one of three). A clause is correct when both answers match the Content table. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 clauses correct on the first attempt. Hovering over a clause and reading the glossary terms is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Freedom at Delphi was a gift from the owner, when the price was usually the enslaved person's own savings. (2) A freed person was immediately and completely free, when many records include a paramone clause. (3) The god's role was decorative, when the sale to the god was the legal mechanism that made re-enslavement impossible. (4) The witnesses and guarantor were formalities, when they were the people who could defend the freedom later. **Instructional Rationale:** Deconstructing a real document form into its working parts is an Analyze task: the learner must decide what each clause does, not just what it says. Asking for the effect of each clause, with protection and limitation as separate answers, makes the learner confront the record's double character. **Content:** A heading above the record reads: "A simplified record in the standard Delphic form. Bracketed words stand for the names that a real record gives. This is a composite, not a translation of one inscription." The record, shown as eight clauses in this order: | # | Clause text shown | Correct name | Correct effect | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | "In the year when [name] was archon, in the month [month]," | Date | Records the facts | Dating by the archon's year made the record findable and checkable by anyone. | | 2 | "[owner's name], son of [father's name], sold to Pythian Apollo" | Sale to the god | Protects the freed person | Once the god owned the person, no human could claim them as property. | | 3 | "a woman named [name], [her homeland] by birth," | Person freed | Records the facts | The record names the person and her origin so that she can be identified later. | | 4 | "for a price of [sum] of silver, and he has received the whole price," | Price | Records the facts | The price was usually the freed person's own savings, and full payment closed the sale. | | 5 | "as [name] entrusted the purchase to the god, on condition that she be free and claimed by no one, doing what she wishes and going where she wishes." | Freedom clause | Protects the freed person | This clause states the freedom itself and forbids anyone to claim her. | | 6 | "Guarantor, according to the law of the city: [name]." | Guarantor | Protects the freed person | The guarantor was legally bound to defend the sale if anyone claimed her as a slave. | | 7 | "[name] shall remain with [owner's name] for as long as he lives, doing what she is told." | Paramone | Limits the freed person's freedom | This condition kept her serving the former owner, often until his death. | | 8 | "Witnesses: the priests of Apollo, [name], [name]." | Witnesses | Protects the freed person | Witnesses could testify to the sale if her freedom was ever challenged. | The eight clause names offered for every clause: Date; Sale to the god; Person freed; Price; Freedom clause; Guarantor; Paramone; Witnesses. The three effects offered for every clause: Protects the freed person; Limits the freed person's freedom; Records the facts. Glossary available on hover: archon, guarantor, witnesses, paramone, manumission, each with the definition given in the chapter section "Manumission Records". **Provenance:** The clause structure, the sale to Pythian Apollo, the entrusting formula, the guarantor, the witnesses, and the paramone condition come from the chapter section "Manumission Records". The wording is a simplified composite of the standard form; the sim must show the heading in Content saying so. **Rules:** - The clauses are always shown in the fixed order 1 to 8. - Each clause has exactly one correct name and one correct effect, as in the Content table. - A clause counts as correct only when both its name and its effect are correct. - Each clause name may be used for more than one clause while answering, but the Check reports every duplicate as wrong for all clauses except the one it fits. - Score = number of correct clauses, from 0 to 8. Mastery is score >= 7 on the first Check. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the whole record, then selects clause 1. 2. For the selected clause, the learner chooses a name and an effect. The clause is marked as answered. 3. The learner repeats step 2 for all eight clauses, in any order. 4. The learner presses Check. Each clause is marked correct or incorrect, and the "Why" text appears for every clause. 5. The learner may change answers on incorrect clauses and press Check again; only the first Check counts toward mastery. 6. After the final Check, a summary line appears under the record: "Four clauses protect her freedom, three record the facts, and one keeps her bound." 7. The learner should notice that the same document both guarantees and limits freedom. **Feedback:** Eight clauses, fixed order, unlimited re-checks. Correct clause: "Correct: [why text]." Incorrect name: "This clause is the [correct name]. [why text]" Incorrect effect only: "Right name, but look again at its effect. [why text]" The score "Clauses correct: n of 8" is shown after each Check. After the second Check, a Show Answers option reveals any remaining correct answers. **Starting State:** The eight clauses of the record, unanswered, with the heading from Content and the question "Which words set her free, and which words keep her bound?" **Chapter Anchors:** More than a thousand manumission records, most from about 200 BCE to 100 CE; the sale to Pythian Apollo; the paramone condition, "often until the owner's death"; eight parts in the chapter's table, the same eight in this record.
